subject: Medford Historical Society and Museum Overview
overview: Host John Petrella interviewed Liz Ammons and John Anderson from the Medford Historical Society and Museum about the organization's history, programs, and community outreach. The guests discussed current exhibits, membership options, and their extensive photograph archives.

items.title: Introduction and Guest Backgrounds
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced volunteer guests Liz Ammons and John Anderson, who described their personal backgrounds and volunteer roles with the Medford Historical Society.

items.title: Museum Operations, Location, and Mission
items.summary: Anderson and Ammons outlined the museum's location at 10 Governors Avenue, its Sunday open hours, free admission, membership pricing, and mission to provide an inclusive history of Medford.

items.title: History of the Medford Historical Society
items.summary: Anderson recounted the society's founding in 1896, the construction of its building in 1916 by Moses Mann, and its mid-century decline and subsequent revivals.

items.title: Museum Exhibits and Civil War Photography Collection
items.summary: Ammons described recent exhibits on local migration and 1776, while Anderson detailed the history and digitization of the museum's extensive Grand Army of the Republic Civil War photograph collection stored at Tufts.

items.title: Community Outreach, Volunteers, and School Programs
items.summary: Ammons and Anderson discussed volunteer opportunities, public lectures at the library, and educational partnerships involving Medford High School interns and elementary school field trips.

items.title: South Medford Racetracks Discussion and Show Closing
items.summary: Petrella and the guests briefly discussed the historic South Medford horse racetracks and research archives before Petrella delivered closing announcements for the program.
